entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This appeal is filed by the injured- appellant/claimant seeking enhancement of compensation being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 30th September 2015 passed in MVC No.1252/2014 on the file of the III-MACT, Ballari (for short "the Tribunal").

2. Brief facts leading to filing of this appeal are that, on 23.04.2014, the claimant and others were gone to as usual coolie work in the field of T.Parameshwara Gouda for carrying the paddy grass to rickyard, when the petitioner carrying paddy grass on his head at about 2:45 p.m., the first respondent, driven his tractor bearing Registration No.KA-34/T-9790 in a high speed and rash and negligent manner endangering to the human life, lost control and ran over the tractor front wheel on the right hand fingers of the claimant.
As a result, the right hand fingers of the claimant broken and sustained grievous injuries and took treatment at the Hospital and spent huge amount for treatment.
The respondent Nos.1 & 2 entered appearance before the Tribunal and opposed the claim petition by filing objections.
They denied the age, income and avocation of the injured.
It is denied that, the accident was caused due to the negligence of the driver of the tractor.
They have sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
4. The Tribunal recorded the evidence of the parties.
The injured examined himself as PW1 and got marked the documents at Exs.P1 to P9.
Respondent No.2 has got examined its Assistant Manager as RW1 and got marked the policy as Ex.R1.

The Tribunal considering the pleading and evidence on record, awarded total compensation in a sum of Rs.2,53,600/- along with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

Being aggrieved, the injured is in this appeal,
seeking higher compensation.

5. Learned counsel Smt. Soubhagya Vakkund for Shri Y.Lakshmikant Reddy appearing for the appellant NC: 2024:KHC-D:11437 submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income of the injured at Rs.5,000/- p.m. and also assessing the disability at 17%, which is contrary to the III-Schedule of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923 and has awarded meagre compensation on all other heads.
Hence she seeks for reassessment of the compensation by consiering the fact that the injured has suffered amputation of three fingers of his right hand, by allowing this appeal.

2 6.

entities.text: Sri.B. Mallikarjuna vs Sri.T. Parameshwara Gouda
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, Sri. S.S, Koliwad, learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2 supports the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal and submits that no evidence was placed before the Tribunal with regard to the income and hence, the assessment of income by the Tribunal is correct.
He further submits that the disability assessed by the Tribunal is as per the schedule to the Act and the question of enhancement of compensation would not arise.
Thus, he seeks to dismiss the appeal.

Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and perused the grounds of appeal, the point that would arise for our consideration in this appeal is as to whether the impugned judgment and award of the tribunal calls for any interference?

8. The parties to the proceedings do not dispute the accident which occurred on 23.04.2014 and also the appellant sustaining grievous injuries on his 3rd, 4th & 5th fingers at proximal Phalyns of right hand.
The wound certificate at Ex.P4 indicates that three fingers of appellant have been amputated.
Taking note of the same, and considering the Schedule-III at Sl.Nos.31 & 35, this Court reassess the disability at 12% to the middle finger, 7% each of the little and ring fingers.
Hence, the total disability would be 26% as against 17% assessed by the Tribunal.

9. The pleading and evidence on record indicate that appellant was agricultural coolie and due to the said accidental injuries, he became disabled to carry out the NC: 2024:KHC-D:11437 same avocation, hence this Court is of the considered view that the entire compensation amount is required to be re-determined and accordingly this Court reassess the compensation by taking note of the oral and documentary evidence on record.
10. The Tribunal has assessed the income of the injured at Rs.5,000/- p.m. admittedly the appellant has not placed on record any cogent and legally acceptable evidence with regard to the income.
Hence, this Court reassess the income of the injured notionally at Rs.7,500/- p.m. placing reliance on the Notional Income Chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

Further,
the Tribunal has applied the appropriate multiplier of 18 based on the age of the injured at the time of accident.

Thus, the injured would be entitled to compensation under the head "loss of future income due to disability" at Rs.4,21,200/- (Rs.7,500/- x 12 x 18 x 26%).
NC: 2024:KHC-D:11437 11.

Taking note of the treatment provided to the injured-appellant/claimant, this Court reassess the compensation awarded under the head "Pain & Suffering"
at Rs.40,000/- as against Rs.30,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.25,000/- towards "loss of amenities and happiness",
which is on the lower side, hence, this Court reassess the same to Rs.30,000/-.
Further, the compensation of Rs.5,000/- awarded by the Tribunal towards "medical & incidental charges" is retained as it is.

3 12.

entities.text: Sri.B. Mallikarjuna vs Sri.T. Parameshwara Gouda
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Further, the appellant has sustained the aforesaid injuries and was admitted as an inpatient in the Hospital, this Court is of the considered view that the injured-appellant/claimant requires at least three month period to recover, so it would be just and proper to award Rs.22,500/- (Rs.7,500/-
x 3 months) under the head "loss of earning during treatment period".
13.

Thus, the injured-appellant/claimant would be entitled to modified compensation on the following heads:
NC: 2024:KHC-D:11437 Particulars Amount (in Rs.) Pain & Suffering Rs.40,000/-
Loss of amenities & happiness Rs.30,000/- Medical & incidental charges Rs.5,000/-
Loss of earning during treatment Rs.22,500/- period Loss of future earning due to Rs.4,21,200/-
 disability  Total Rs.5,18,700/-
14.
Thus, the injured-appellant/claimant would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.5,18,700/- as against Rs.2,53,600/- awarded by the Tribunal.

15. In the result, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal stands allowed in part.

(ii) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that the injured-appellant/claimant would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.5,18,700/- as against Rs.2,53,600/- awarded by the Tribunal.

(iii) The enhanced compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of payment.

NC: 2024:KHC-D:11437 (iv) The respondent - Insurance Company to pay the entire compensation amount along with interest to the injured-appellant/claimant within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
(v) Apportionment, deposit and disbursement shall be made as per the award of the Tribunal.
(vi) Draw modified award accordingly.
